description: This bar chart illustrates the relationship between Fleiss Kappa values and ambiguity metrics, displaying two separate charts side-by-side. In both charts, the horizontal axis represents categories of ambiguity, with labels indicating ambiguity standard deviation in the left chart (0.0, 0.47, 0.82, 0.94) and maximum ambiguity in the right chart (1, 2, 3). The vertical axis, labeled “Fleiss Kappa,” has a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 0.9, with tick marks at 0.2 intervals. The left chart consists of four dark teal bars, sorted from left to right according to increasing ambiguity standard deviation; the bar corresponding to 0.0 ambiguity standard deviation reaches approximately 0.88 on the Fleiss Kappa scale, while the bar for 0.94 ambiguity standard deviation reaches approximately 0.24. The right chart also contains four dark teal bars, sorted from left to right according to increasing maximum ambiguity; the bar corresponding to maximum ambiguity of 1 reaches approximately 0.89 on the Fleiss Kappa scale, and the bar for maximum ambiguity of 3 reaches approximately 0.23. No bars are visually emphasized through shading, bolding, outlining, or annotation.
caption_used: Inter-annotator agreement compared to sample-level ambiguity standard deviation and sample-level maximum ambiguity values. The left chart shows Fleiss Kappa values decreasing steadily as Ambiguity Std increases, with values approximately 0.88, 0.46, 0.12, and 0.24 for categories 0.0, 0.47, 0.82, and 0.94, respectively. The right chart demonstrates a similar trend, with Fleiss Kappa values declining from 0.89 to 0.46 and then to 0.12 for Max Ambiguity categories 1, 2, and 3. The data suggests a consistent negative correlation between ambiguity measures and inter-annotator agreement.
